title: Kingdom of Champasak
capsule: The Kingdom of Champasak was a Lao kingdom in the southern Mekong region, founded in 1713 when the grandson of King Sourigna Vongsa, Nokasad, established an independent realm after the dissolution of Lan Xang. The kingdom controlled the strategic confluence of the Mekong and Se Done rivers near the Khmer ceremonial complex of Wat Phu, and its rulers alternated between independence and vassalage under Siam following Taksin's invasion in 1778. French colonial expansion incorporated Champasak into French Laos in 1904, with its territories redistributed between French Cambodia and Annam; the last ruling family retained nominal prestige into the twentieth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core along the southern Mekong is established in Lao chronicles and French colonial records, but frontier boundaries—especially with Cambodia—are imprecise before the French imposed fixed colonial borders.
